label: PLURAL_REASON_1: Plural W F relates a world, a class of facts and a fact: G w Xs f says that at w…
definition: Plural W F relates a world, a class of facts and a fact: G w Xs f says that at w the facts Xs are together admitted as a reason why f obtains. PNecessitating says that at each accessible world where all Xs hold, f holds. PContrast says that at each accessible world where f fails, some member of Xs fails. PDistribution says that reasons for an aggregate are reasons for each conjunct. PartIrreflexive says that no contingent fact is among its own reasons. Each is a separate hypothesis, and none is built into G.
note: Analyst vocabulary for #365, because no one conjunct necessitates an aggregate. Dasgupta's talk of some facts together grounding a conjunction (DASGUPTA-MR-GROUND-CONJUNCTS) motivates the plural form, but G is the general reason relation and not his notion of ground, and PContrast is not attributed to any source. See docs/notes/bccf-sources-365.md.
